newsitem.title: USA: Frisch's says investors win board seats.
newsitem.headline: Frisch's says investors win board seats.

text.p: Frisch's Restaurants Inc said Wednesday that new investors Barry Nussbaum and Jerry Ruyan defeated two incumbents on its board of directors.

Two other incumbents, including chairman Jack Maier, were re-elected, Frisch's said. The eight-member board now has four inside and four independent directors, a Frisch's spokesman said in a telephone interview.

Nussbaum's and Ruyan's Wolverine Partners mailed its own proxy with its slate of four nominees to shareholders after Wolverine bought about 5.5 percent of the Big Boy restaurant chain's common stock in July.
Wolverine said then that the company's management, led by the Maier family, was not maximizing shareholder value.
"The shareholders have expressed their will," chairman Jack Maier said. "I pledge to work with the new directors for the benefit of all investors in Frisch's."
Wolverine nominees Thomas Doan and Arthur Engel lost.
A Wolverine proposal which passed will require a majority of the board be non-management but a second proposal, to eliminate staggered terms, was defeated, Frisch's said.
The vote was at Frisch's annual meeting Oct 7, but Frisch's had said a final tally would take several days.
At its fiscal yearend June 2, Frisch's had 103 Big Boy restaurants and two Quality Hotels.
